elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.2(a): "In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, no termination payment (the "Termination Payment"), liquidated damages or penalty shall be payable by the Company to HDI." The Net Sales-based formula (twelve months' Net Sales less $800,000, divided by two) is deleted, and no other Customer-payable penalty or minimum fee appears in the cited text.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind, so the restriction has nothing to bite on (preferred outcome is stronger than the fallback).

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee survives 4.2(a), so no cap is required; the eliminated formula was the only Customer-payable termination charge.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: 4.2(a) as revised states that no termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty is payable by the Company, so there is no liquidated amount to designate as sole.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative sentence in 4.2(a) affirmatively bars any Customer-payable termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty, and the offending Net Sales formula is struck rather than merely promised in the comment.

Minimality holds: only the payment-formula sentence in 4.2(a) was rewritten; the ninety-day notice/Termination Date mechanics in 4.1, the fee construct in 3.1, and the Customer-favourable "without penalty" right in 1.6 are untouched, and no survival tails, damages categories or procedures were added. The added words "liquidated damages or penalty" sit squarely within the single preferred element rather than being an extra requirement.

Intent is preserved: the defined term "Termination Payment" is retained in 4.2(a), so the retained 4.2(c) instalment mechanic ("The Termination Payment, if any") and any other reference in 4.2(b) are not left dangling, and the "if any" qualifier prevents contradiction with the new prohibition.

Housekeeping note (not a defect requiring repair): because the defined term now labels a payment that can never arise, 4.2(c) is inert surplusage; if counsel prefers a cleaner section, 4.2(c) could be deleted in the same pass, but retaining it is the lower-touch, minimal option.

Confirm on the full section that 4.2(b) does not independently compute or preserve a Company-payable amount (it was not rendered here); if it does, the deletion must extend to that subsection to avoid an internally inconsistent retained sentence.
